title: add jsonschema response_format strict mode + improved errors (OpenAI compat)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: customers expect a predictable structured output API that is OpenAI-compatible. This PR implements a strict mode for the existing response_format=jsonschema endpoint so that model responses are validated against the provided JSON Schema, and clear, actionable error messages are returned when validation fails. It also harmonizes behavior with the OpenAI compatibility layer (field names, error codes, and streaming behavior). Summary of changes: 1) Add `strict` option to response_format/jsonschema that enforces schema validation before returning final response. When strict=true, the server will attempt basic correction heuristics (whitespace trimming, JSON extraction from surrounding text) and will return a structured validation error if correction fails. 2) New error payload format aligned with OpenAI-style errors: code, type, message, details (array of strings). 3) Streaming: for strict mode, partial tokens are streamed as before but final validation occurs at end-of-stream; if validation fails and correction heuristics succeed we patch and emit a final validated object; if not, we send a final event containing the structured error with http 400 for non-OpenAI-compat endpoints and a compat-coded error for OpenAI endpoints. 4) Added server-side validation hooks and a pluggable validator interface to support alternate JSON Schema libs and future strictness levels. 5) Docs and SDK updates: Python/TS SDKs now expose response_format.strict and the new error type; examples updated. 6) Extensive tests and fuzz cases for edge-cases (malformed JSON in text, multi-line responses, extra wrapper text). Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged (strict=false). The OpenAI compatibility mode will translate Redwood errors to the closer OpenAI style when the compatibility header is present. Implementation notes: - Validator runs in the request post-processing path; we reuse the existing streaming buffer but keep a capped parsed-buffer size to avoid unbounded memory for large outputs. - Correction heuristics are intentionally conservative: they only try to extract a single top-level JSON object/array and apply simple fixes (trailing commas removal, quote balancing). Any aggressive mutation is disabled by default and requires opt-in. - Added metrics: jsonschema.validation.success, jsonschema.validation.failure, jsonschema.validation.latency_ms, jsonschema.corrections.applied. - Feature gated via runtime flag: response_format.strict can be enabled per-tenant via config and is off by default for hosted customers until metrics/compat testing completes. Related: ENG-4821 (design), SUP-128 (customer incident motivating stricter errors).
commits: feat(api): add strict flag to response_format/jsonschema and validator hooks
fix(streaming): defer final validation until end-of-stream; add final error event path
perf: cap buffer size for streaming schema validation
test: add unit/fuzz tests for schema strict mode and heuristics
docs: update structured-output and openai-compat docs and examples
files_changed: service/api/response_format/jsonschema_handler.rs: add strict handling, validator integration, error mapping
service/runtime/stream_buffer.rs: expose capped buffer and finalization hook
service/compat/openai_mapper.rs: map redwood error -> openai error shapes
sdk/python/redwood/api.py: expose response_format.strict in client call signature and examples
sdk/typescript/src/structured_output.ts: typings + example for strict mode
docs/reference/response_format.md: document strict behavior, error codes, metrics
review_comments: Lucas Nguyen: Please confirm streaming semantics - we should not block token streaming for large outputs. Aisha: Streaming unchanged; validation only at end-of-stream. If validation fails we emit a final error event and close the stream (compat path included).
Marta Jensen: Can we make heuristics configurable per-tenant? Aisha: Yes, heuristics are behind a per-tenant config toggle; defaults conservative.
Kai O'Connor: Need more tests covering nested schema edge-cases (oneOf/anyOf). Aisha: Added additional fuzz tests and explicit oneOf/anyOf tests in tests/jsonschema/strict_mode_tests.rs.

Security review (internal comment): Ensure validator lib is pinned and sandboxed to prevent DoS from complex schemas. Aisha: We added a schema complexity cap and runtime guard (max keywords and depth).
release_notes: Added response_format=jsonschema strict mode (opt-in) with conservative correction heuristics and OpenAI-compatible structured error responses. Default behavior unchanged. New metrics exposed for validation success/failure and applied corrections. SDKs updated to surface strict flag and error shapes.
notes_for_ops: Strict mode enabled per-tenant via runtime flag. Monitor jsonschema.validation.failure rate and latency; enable heuristics only after validating low failure rates in staging. Watch memory usage for requests with very large streams (buffer cap enforced).
changelog_entry: 2025-02-20: response_format=jsonschema: added strict mode and improved OpenAI-compatible error reporting (Aisha Patel).
user_facing_changes: API: new optional flag response_format.strict (boolean). SDKs: python/typescript clients expose strict param. Docs: structured output guide updated with examples and error formats.
support_guidance: When customers see validation errors, advise them to: 1) supply stricter schemas where possible, 2) enable heuristics if acceptable, 3) use exact matching in schema (avoid oneOf if not needed). For immediate mitigation, recommend setting strict=false or using the non-strict path.
qa_notes: Added unit, integration and fuzz tests. Test matrix covers streaming and non-streaming models, OpenAI compat header on/off, and various schema complexities. Manual QA validated sample apps in redwood-examples with strict=true and strict=false.
implementation_risks: Possible increased latency at end-of-stream for very large outputs due to validation; mitigated by buffer cap and async validation instrumentation. Edge-case schemas (deep recursion) may cause validator timeouts; we added complexity limits and fallbacks.
